# Kauffman — Iterants, Fermions and the Dirac Equation (arXiv v2, 2014)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** Louis H. Kauffman, “Iterants, Fermions and the Dirac Equation,” arXiv:1406.1929v2 [quant-ph], revised June 14, 2014, https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1406.1929.

**Shortened note:** Kauffman, “Iterants.”

**Bibliography:** Kauffman, Louis H. “Iterants, Fermions and the Dirac Equation.” arXiv:1406.1929v2 [quant-ph]. Revised June 14, 2014. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1406.1929.

## Essay use

Kauffman provides an explicit iterant construction linking two shifted views of an alternating process to \(i\) and \(-i\). His own non-trivial-kernel discussion limits any attempt to treat one iterant representation as uniquely privileged.

**Claim boundary:** this is a formal construction in a specific preprint. It neither establishes QL, consciousness, memory, the metaphysical primacy of time, nor a unique meaning of \(i\). The arXiv record notes substantial overlap with earlier Kauffman manuscripts; this source selects v2 and its fixed PDF pages 27–28 only.

<a id="kauffman-2014-iterants-fermions-dirac-arxiv-q001"></a>
## Passage card — `kauffman-2014-iterants-fermions-dirac-arxiv-q001` — alternating process and temporal shift
^kauffman-2014-iterants-fermions-dirac-arxiv-q001

> “Given an iterant [a, b], we can think of [b, a] as the same process with a shift of one time step. These two iterant views, seen as points of view of an alternating process, will become the square roots of negative unity, i and −i.”

- **Locator:** PDF p. 28/54, §6, “The Square Root of Minus One is a Clock”; follows the period-two `+1/−1` oscillation and precedes `[a,b]η = η[b,a]`.
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manual transcription checked against official arXiv v2 PDF page image and embedded text; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted.

- **Use boundary:** establishes an iterant construction only; it does not establish QL, consciousness, memory, or a unique metaphysical interpretation of \(i\).

<a id="kauffman-2014-iterants-fermions-dirac-arxiv-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `kauffman-2014-iterants-fermions-dirac-arxiv-q002` — representation non-uniqueness
^kauffman-2014-iterants-fermions-dirac-arxiv-q002

> “Here we have seen that the fact that the kernel of the mapping p is non-trivial means that there is often a choice in making an iterant representation for a given matrix or for an algebra of matrices.”

- **Locator:** PDF p. 27/54, end of §5, following the non-trivial-kernel construction from iterant algebra to matrices.
